ambiguities.text: The specification uses 'more than' MAX_CODE_SIZE, implying contracts of exactly 24576 bytes are valid, but this boundary case could be clearer.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Confirm that code length <= 24576 is valid, and code length > 24576 triggers failure (strict inequality).

ambiguities.text: The specification does not address what happens if the init code itself exceeds the size limit during deployment.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the limit applies only to the returned deployment bytecode, not the init code.

implicit_assumptions.description: The MAX_CODE_SIZE limit is applied consistently across all client implementations.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Consensus failures if clients disagree on valid contract sizes.

implicit_assumptions.description: 24576 bytes is sufficient for most legitimate contract use cases.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Developers may need to use proxy patterns or contract splitting, increasing complexity.

implicit_assumptions.description: Without size limits, an attacker could deploy contracts large enough to cause DoS conditions.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If there are other limiting factors (gas cost), the attack may not be practical anyway.

implicit_assumptions.description: Block producers will not include invalid transactions that exceed size limits.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Invalid blocks would be rejected by validating nodes, causing network churn.
